title: introduce-low-cardinality-metric-projection-and-query-cost-guardrails
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce low-cardinality metric projection to reduce dashboard/query cost and a query-cost guardrail layer that prevents expensive ad-hoc queries from impacting production observability storage. Backfilled lightweight projections for key token-cost and latency metrics. Feature rolled out behind flag with canary tenants.
description:
Summary:
This PR adds a low-cardinality projection path for high-cardinality observability signals and a query-cost guardrail service that detects and blocks queries likely to cause excessive storage or compute usage. Motivation: dashboards and ad-hoc analysis over token-level labels (tenant_id, route, model_version, prompt_hash) have been creating high-cardinality queries that spike query billing and increase latency for the observability pipeline. Instead of removing signal, we project a derived, low-cardinality set of metrics that preserve SLO-relevant information while reducing cardinality and storage footprint.

Design & changes made:
- Introduce metric-projection module (observability/projections/low_cardinality.py) that consumes the normalized token telemetry and emits a compact set of derived metrics (per-tenant aggregated token_cost_bucket, median_token_latency_bin, route_cohort_id).
- Add an indexer that maps high-cardinality label combinations into ephemeral cohort ids using an LRU-backed cohort registry to keep cardinality bounded. Cohort registry is sharded and uses consistent hashing to remain stable across restarts.
- Query-cost guardrail service (observability/query_guard/guard.py) that computes a cost estimate for incoming queries (based on time range, cardinality hints, and aggregation complexity) and either permits, throttles, or rejects queries. Default policy rejects queries above threshold unless run with preview=true and the user has canary permission.
- Console/dashboard changes: new "Low-cardinality Preview" toggle for dashboards and a "Cost Estimate" line above long-running query panels showing projected cost units.
- Migration: backfill job (observability/migrations/backfill_lowcard.py) to generate derived metrics for the last 14 days for high-volume tenants. Backfill runs as a batched k8s job with rate-limiting and health checks.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for projection logic, integration test against a small observability dataset, and docs page for operators covering thresholds, rollout, and rollback.

Why this is different from existing approaches:
- Instead of coarse downsampling, projection preserves cohort-aware signals that let SRE/product teams diagnose regressions without exploding metric cardinality.
- The guardrail is a proactive cost estimate instead of post-hoc rate limiting; it gives users feedback and a preview path to validate queries safely.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated: flag observability.low_card_projection (off).
2) Enable for internal/canary tenants only; run backfill for those tenants.
3) Monitor storage, query latency, and alert volume for 72 hours.
4) If metrics stable, expand to 10% of tenants with automated ramp.
5) Full-on default after two weeks and final approval from SRE.

Testing / validation:
- Unit tests cover projection boundary conditions, cohort registry eviction semantics, and guardrail estimator correctness.
- Integration test uses synthetic token telemetry to assert 5-10x reduction in time-series cardinality on average for test tenants.
- Backfill dry-run validated against staging data; job includes a safety throttle if query budget exceeded.

Operational notes and rollback:
- Flag can be toggled immediately to stop projection and revert to original metrics.
- Backfill writes are idempotent; rollback deletes projected metrics for the last 14 days from the derived metrics table.
- Guardrail has an audit log; self-service preview is allowed for users with canary role to validate queries without system-wide impact.

Related work: ENG-1427 (metric-cardinality task), ENG-1499 (dashboard cost playbook).

review_thread: Rohit: Nice approach. A couple questions: How do we ensure cohort ids don't leak PII? Please add deterministic hashing and salt per-cluster.
Maya: Added salted hashing with cluster-unique salt; updated cohort_registry and unit tests (see commit b7d4e02).
Avery: Guardrail estimator looks conservative; can we expose a telemetry signal so users see historical cost of similar queries?
Maya: Added historical hint endpoint + example UI line; estimator still uses worst-case until we have more telemetry.
Priya: Please add an e2e that verifies the backfill won't exceed query budget and that the job respects the rate limit.
Maya: Added rate-limited backfill with a dry-run flag and integrated e2e (commit d2f5a88).
Rohit: Approve after test coverage added.
Priya: Approved and queued for merge.

merge_summary: Merged by Priya Kapoor on 2026-02-18 via squash-merge. Commit message: introduce low-cardinality metric projection and query-cost guardrails. Backfill scheduled as a post-merge job for canary tenants.
notes: Operator doc includes recommended thresholds; SRE will tune guardrail threshold for first 72h. Observability cost dashboards should show immediate drop in high-cardinality series for canary tenants.
manual_steps: 1) Enable flag observability.low_card_projection for target tenant. 2) Run backfill with dry-run=false for tenant id. 3) Monitor observability.metrics.cardinality and queries.cost_units.
